content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT NEEDS TO HEAR ABOUT {{YOUR OWN}} HEALTH
facts: **Eat standing up if you have to** – a rushed meal is still better than a skipped one when you're running on broken sleep.
**Stack your vitamin D with your coffee** – 1 habit you'll actually remember beats a pill routine you forget by week two.
**Nap in 20-minute blocks** – anything longer leaves you groggier, anything shorter won't touch your sleep debt.
**Keep a water bottle on the changing table** – breastfeeding and chasing a toddler both drain fluids faster than you notice.
**Let the dishes sit, not your blood pressure** – 10 minutes of sitting down and breathing does more for you than a spotless sink.
**Batch-cook protein on Sundays** – having cooked chicken thighs or beans ready means you won't default to crackers at 8pm.
**Ask for a 1-hour solo walk weekly** – it's not selfish, it's the minimum most new parents need to stay regulated.
**Check your own mood, not just the baby's** – persistent sadness or numbness past 2 weeks postpartum deserves a real conversation with a doctor.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
New parent life makes even basic habits feel impossible, so small swaps matter more than perfect routines. Take vitamin D stacked with your morning coffee: pairing a new habit with an existing one (called habit stacking) makes it far more likely to stick when your brain is foggy from lack of sleep. Batch-cooking protein like chicken thighs or beans on a slower day means your blood sugar stays steadier through the week instead of crashing from grabbing whatever's closest. And that 20-minute nap isn't random — it's short enough to avoid deep sleep inertia, so you wake up actually more alert instead of groggier than before. Everyone's situation looks different, so take what fits your week.
